title: Grade 11 Physics — Work, Energy and Power
description: Chapter 6: work-energy theorem, kinetic and potential energy, conservation, power
subject: physics

questions.question: Work done by a force F on an object displaced by d at angle θ to the force is:
questions.explanation: W = F·d·cosθ. Only the component of force along the direction of displacement does work. If θ = 90°, W = 0 (no work done — e.g., carrying a bag horizontally).

questions.question: What is the work done if the force is perpendicular to displacement?
questions.explanation: W = Fd cos90° = Fd × 0 = 0. The centripetal force in circular motion does no work because it is always perpendicular to velocity (= perpendicular to displacement).

questions.question: The work-energy theorem states that:
options: Work done equals change in potential energy
Net work done on an object equals its change in kinetic energy (W_net = ΔKE)
questions.explanation: W_net = ΔKE = ½mv₂² - ½mv₁². This connects kinematics and dynamics — work done by the net force changes the kinetic energy.

questions.question: The kinetic energy of a body of mass m moving with velocity v is:
questions.explanation: KE = ½mv². This can be derived from the work-energy theorem: W = ∫F·dx = ∫ma·dx = ∫mv·(dv/dx)·dx = ∫mv dv = ½mv².

questions.question: If the speed of a body is doubled, its kinetic energy becomes:
questions.explanation: KE = ½mv². If v → 2v, KE → ½m(2v)² = ½m·4v² = 4 × ½mv² = 4KE. Kinetic energy is proportional to the SQUARE of speed.

questions.question: Power is defined as:
options: Work done per unit time (P = W/t)
questions.explanation: P = W/t = F·v (instantaneous power = force × velocity). The SI unit is Watt (W) = Joule/second. 1 horsepower ≈ 746 W.

questions.question: The gravitational potential energy of mass m at height h above a reference level is:
questions.explanation: PE = mgh. This is the work done against gravity to raise the mass from the reference level to height h. It converts to kinetic energy as the object falls.

questions.question: A ball of mass m is dropped from height h. What fraction of its total mechanical energy is kinetic energy when it has fallen h/2?
questions.explanation: Total energy = mgh. At height h/2: PE = mg(h/2) = mgh/2. KE = Total - PE = mgh - mgh/2 = mgh/2 = ½ of total energy.

questions.question: A spring compressed by x stores potential energy E. If compression doubles to 2x, the energy stored becomes:
questions.explanation: Spring PE = ½kx². If x → 2x: PE = ½k(2x)² = 4(½kx²) = 4E. Spring energy is proportional to the square of compression/extension.

questions.question: What is a conservative force?
options: A force that always acts in the same direction
A force for which work done depends only on initial and final positions, not on the path taken
A force that never does negative work
A force that is always constant in magnitude
questions.explanation: Conservative forces (gravity, spring force, electrostatic force) have two key properties: (1) work done is path-independent; (2) work done in a closed loop = 0. They allow the definition of potential energy.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a conservative force?
questions.explanation: Friction is non-conservative — work done against friction is path-dependent (longer path = more work done) and cannot be recovered as potential energy. It converts mechanical energy to heat irreversibly.

questions.question: The principle of conservation of mechanical energy states that in the absence of non-conservative forces:
options: Total mechanical energy (KE + PE) remains constant
Potential energy equals kinetic energy at all times
Energy is created by gravity as objects fall
questions.explanation: When only conservative forces act, KE + PE = constant. As a ball falls, PE decreases and KE increases by the same amount. Total mechanical energy is unchanged.

questions.question: In a perfectly inelastic collision:
options: Both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved
Momentum is conserved, but kinetic energy is lost (converted to heat/sound/deformation)
Neither momentum nor kinetic energy is conserved
questions.explanation: In a perfectly inelastic collision, objects stick together. Momentum is always conserved (if no external forces). Maximum kinetic energy is lost — the minimum consistent with momentum conservation.

questions.question: An engine of power 10 kW moves a car up a smooth incline (sin θ = 0.1) at constant speed. What is the speed? (m = 1000 kg, g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: At constant speed, P = Fv. Force needed = mgsinθ = 1000×10×0.1 = 1000 N. v = P/F = 10000/1000 = 10 m/s.

questions.question: The efficiency of a machine is defined as:
questions.explanation: Efficiency η = (Useful output / Total input) × 100%. No real machine is 100% efficient because friction and other non-conservative forces always dissipate some energy as heat.

questions.question: A particle is displaced from A to B under a constant force of 10 N at 60° to the displacement of 5 m. Work done = ?
The dimensional formula for work/energy is:
questions.explanation: Work = Force × Distance = [MLT⁻²] × [L] = [ML²T⁻²]. This is the same dimension as energy (joule). Power = Work/Time = [ML²T⁻³].

questions.question: Which statement about potential energy is correct?
options: Potential energy depends only on the position of the object (in a conservative force field)
Potential energy can never be zero
Potential energy equals kinetic energy at the highest point of any motion
questions.explanation: Potential energy is a function of position only in a conservative force field. It can be negative (e.g., gravitational PE relative to a reference below the object), and can be zero at chosen reference points.

questions.question: 1 horsepower is approximately equal to:
questions.explanation: 1 hp ≈ 746 W. This unit was defined by James Watt based on how much work a horse could sustain over a long period. It is still used to rate car engines and electric motors.

questions.question: A 2 kg ball is thrown vertically upward with v = 20 m/s. What is its maximum height? (g = 10 m/s², ignore air resistance)
questions.explanation: Using energy conservation: KE = PE at max height. ½mv² = mgh. h = v²/2g = 400/20 = 20 m. All kinetic energy converts to gravitational potential energy.
